data.narrative:
Mariana Minerals is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $95M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Stage-progression methodology was the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $95M as a base value proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, this method implies a valuation of $190M. Peer-median analysis was not viable; while eight same-sector comparables exist, none met the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or comparable valuation tier—a minimum of three datapoints is required for statistical validity in peer triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, with a median point of $190M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result, accounting for variance in step-up timing and magnitude across frontier-tech raises. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable same-stage transactions in the narrow Climate & Energy subsector and reliance on a single methodological pillar. Any valuation conclusion should be stress-tested against company-specific metrics (burn rate, runway, technical milestones) and forward guidance on next-round timing and capital needs.
